text: When a folded symmetric sky130 FIR misses 200 MHz by ~0.2% with the accumulator adder on the critical path, do not trim acc_width 32→29 to shorten the carry—it saved 167 LUTs but rerouted the g_mac[1].hm[8] path through an and2_4/fa_1 segment and dropped Fmax 199.62→192.22 MHz (-7.4 MHz), so keep 32 bits and target the operand mux/MAC count instead.

When a sky130 folded FIR at fold=4 is timing-limited by the symmetric pre-adder carry chain in the operand path, drop symmetry and increase the fold to 8 so the pre-adder disappears while the same two multipliers remain, raising Fmax from 192.22 to 203.2 MHz and cutting 246 LUTs.

For a sky130 folded FIR pinned near 200 MHz by the 12x12 multiplier's internal carry-save/prefix reduction, collapse to M=1 (fold=16) with acc_width=28 and no sum tree, gaining +4.7 MHz (203.2 to 207.9) and -1458 LUTs (3285 to 1827) because deleting extra multipliers/accumulators/sum tree leaves the limiting multiplier path unchanged.

For a folded FIR on sky130 with fold=16, M=1, acc_width=28 that is feasible at 207.86 MHz but only ~4% margin and adder/MAC-critical, skip the extra post-multiplier pipe_mul stage: it drops Fmax to 207.74 MHz and adds 55 LUTs with DSP unchanged, because the 4.7 ns MAC carry/reduction path is not split enough to let the resizer recover area.

When the folded sky130 FIR is already feasible at fold=16 with one 12x12 multiplier and its critical path is the multiplier's own 5-deep carry-reduce chain (5.24 ns), do not halve coefficients to 8 and go symmetric (fold=8, acc_width=29) to save resources, because it adds 575 LUTs (1882→2457) and costs 1.2 MHz (207.74→206.56) while leaving that multiplier path untouched; keep fold=16 and seek FF/cell-count reductions instead.

When a sky130 folded FIR with symmetric fold=8, acc_width=29, and reg_in is adder-limited at 206.56 MHz, go non-symmetric at fold=16 with acc_width=28 and reg_in=false to keep MAC count while removing the pre-adder/input FFs from the accumulator path, gaining 1.2 MHz (207.78 MHz) and saving 624 LUTs at DSP=0.

On sky130 folded FIR at 207.8 MHz with the critical path FF g_mac[0].hm[3] -> and2_1 -> fa_1 -> product register, do not remove pipe_mul to save ~80 LUT when it already sits after pq and cannot split the intra-multiplier ripple: merging the array output into the 28-bit accumulator ripple drops Fmax to 186.7 MHz (-21.1 MHz) and loses feasibility.

When a folded FIR on sky130 is timing-limited inside the single 12x12 multiplier's carry-save array (FF -> and2_1 -> 5x fa_1, 5.65 ns, only 186.7 MHz after fold=16/acc_width=28/reg_in removal, and no IR field can split a multiplier), adding multiplier pipeline registers (pipe_mul 0 -> 2) to break the reduction/accumulator chain makes the design feasible at 205.2 MHz for +126 LUT and no DSP change.

In a sky130 folded FIR whose 12×12 multiplier array is the ~4.7 ns critical path and pipe_mul stages after the array give no Fmax gain, keep the pipe_in operand register despite its ~13 FF (4%) cost, because deleting it exposes the 16:1 tap mux to the multiplier input and drops Fmax 205.2→172.3 MHz (-32.9 MHz, +84 LUT), losing feasibility.

When a folded symmetric FIR on sky130 misses 200 MHz by only 0.2% (199.62 MHz) with the critical path entirely inside the 12x12 multiplier (g_mac[1].hm[8] through ~5-deep fa_1 carry chain/CPA to the product register), do not change pipe_mul from 1 to 2 while cutting acc_width from 32 to 29, because the extra register stage did not split that multiplier-internal path and Fmax fell to 192.66 MHz (−7.0 MHz) while saving only 62 LUTs.

When a folded symmetric FIR on sky130 is timing-limited near 200 MHz (192.7 MHz) with the multiplier combinational segment too deep, add a third multiplier pipeline stage to cut each segment to ~1/3 of the FA-array depth, raising Fmax to 203.6 MHz (+10.9 MHz) for +10 LUTs and 0 DSPs.

When a folded symmetric FIR on sky130 misses 200 MHz by only 0.2% (199.62 MHz) with the critical path wholly inside the fabric multiplier (operand register through the 12x12 partial-product FA carry chain to the product register, 5.52 ns), raise multiplier pipelining from 1 to 3 stages and trim the accumulator width from 32 to 29 to reach 203.56 MHz (+3.9 MHz, 5.46 ns) while cutting 52 LUTs and keeping DSPs at 0, because splitting the FA-array combinational depth shortens the dominant path and the 3 excess accumulator bits were pure area/ripple.

When a folded symmetric FIR on sky130 is area-heavy from duplicated 12x12 fabric multiplier arrays and pipe_mul=3 internal FFs but throughput is unconstrained, double the fold from 4 to 8 and cut pipe_mul from 3 to 1 to collapse to one multiplier, removing 1189 LUTs and raising Fmax from 203.56 to 206.56 MHz because the raw full-adder depth still fits the 5 ns period.

When a sky130 folded symmetric FIR is already at the 1-multiplier/29-bit accumulator structural floor and the critical path is the internal 12x12 multiplier carry-save chain (xm[8] FF -> and2_1 -> fa_1/ha_2 -> pq FF at 5.32 ns/206.6 MHz, ~3% margin), do not drop the 12-FF input boundary register to save area: it yielded only +1.1 MHz to 207.7 MHz while costing +21 LUTs (2457 to 2478) and no feasibility change, because the path starts at the pipe_in operand register, not the sample boundary.

When a sky130 folded FIR is feasible at ~208 MHz with the critical path inside the one physical multiplier's FA/CSA array after pipe_mul, don't spend area on reg_in; remove the 8 12-bit symmetric pre-adders (symmetric=false, acc_width 29→28) and if the fold doubles to 16 add one multiplier pipeline register (pipe_mul=2), which held Fmax at 207.74 MHz while cutting 596 LUTs at 0 DSPs because the pre-adder/mux logic is off that multiplier-internal path.

When a folded FIR on sky130 is feasible at 207.7 MHz with its 5.24 ns critical path starting at the multiplier operand register, disabling the boundary input register (reg_in) saves only 3 LUTs and 0 DSPs for a 2.5 MHz Fmax drop to 205.2 MHz, so use it only as an area trim when more than 2.5 MHz of timing margin is expendable, since the critical path still starts at the operand register.

When a sky130 folded FIR is feasible but only ~2.5% above the 200-MHz floor with the critical path in the DSP-combinational multiplier reduction/sign glue, increase pipe_mul from 2 to 3 to bisect the ~1.4-ns post-array logic, yielding 205.23→210.29 MHz (+5.1 MHz), -20 LUTs, and no DSP change.

When a sky130 folded FIR with one 12x12 multiplier is feasible at 210 MHz with only ~5.2 MHz margin and the critical path runs through the multiplier adder, dropping one product-register stage saves 26 LUTs but drops Fmax by 2.5 MHz to 207.8 MHz, so keep the stage if margin is under ~5 MHz.

On a folded FIR whose 5.25 ns critical path is entirely inside the multiplier (operand FF xm → 5-deep fa_1 array → product reg pq) and whose area is already minimal, do not delete the ~24-bit product pipeline register to save ~27 FF/~566 um2, because it stretches the multiplier combinational delay to 5.65 ns, dropping Fmax 207.78→186.68 MHz (−21.1 MHz) and losing feasibility for only 80 LUTs saved.

When a sky130 FIR is timing-limited by the folded DSP-combinational carry/adder path (5.65 ns, 186.7 MHz, critical cell fa_1), changing fold from 16 to 8 with a registered 2-way sum tree and multiplier pipelining halves tap/coefficient mux depth and removes the adder from the critical path, raising Fmax to 206.5 MHz (+19.8 MHz) at +1484 LUTs and no DSP change.

When a folded symmetric FIR on sky130 is already at the ~205 MHz multiplier-internal ceiling (204.7 MHz, 5429 LUTs, 0 DSPs), keep the multiplier output/product register rather than changing pipe_mul to [1,0], because removing it exposes the fa_1 carry-propagate adder on the critical path (5.47->5.88 ns) and costs 22.4 MHz (204.7->182.3 MHz), losing feasibility for only 84 LUTs saved.

In sky130 folded symmetric FIR timing-limited at 182.3 MHz by the multiplier FA carry chain, set pipe_mul=1 and reg_in=false to split that carry chain and drop off-path boundary FFs, gaining 23.0 MHz (to 205.3 MHz) for +393 LUT and 0 DSP as the adder leaves the critical path.

On sky130 folded symmetric FIRs already feasible at ~205 MHz with the 5.47 ns critical path entirely inside the DSP combinational FA/CSA array and throughput pinned at 0.5 samples/cycle, drop the 12-FF input register to trim area, accepting the measured ~2.5 MHz fmax cost while staying above 200 MHz because that register is off the multiplier-internal path.

When a sky130 folded symmetric FIR is feasible at ~205 MHz with its critical path entirely inside the 12x12 multiplier and fold-independent, skip removing input-boundary reg_in for area because it only shifted Fmax +0.6 MHz to 205.3 MHz while LUT grew 309, as reg_in is off that multiplier-internal path and cannot unlock higher throughput—only fold=1/transposed or multiplier restructuring can.

When a sky130 FIR is feasible at fold=2 symmetric but stuck at 205.3 MHz with a 5.42 ns critical path inside the 12x12 multiplier carry-save array and only 0.5 samples/cycle, switch to fold=1 non-symmetric transposed form with pipe_mul=2 and reg_in=true, dropping the 8 12-bit pre-adders, to reach 1.0 sample/cycle and gain +7.9 MHz (213.16 MHz) while cutting 53 LUTs.

When a sky130 FIR at fold=2 is feasible at 204.67 MHz but capped at 0.5 samples/cycle with a 5.47 ns critical path inside the 12x12 carry-save multiplier array, break the fold to 1 with an asymmetric transposed structure by removing the shared pre-adder (acc_width 29->28), adding a multiplier pipe (pipe_mul 1->2), and disabling reg_in/sum_tree/pipe_in, yielding 1 sample/cycle at 205.46 MHz (+0.8 MHz) for +530 LUTs and 0 DSPs because the multiplier operand no longer passes through the shared pre-adder and the mult->add->reg segment remains local (4.69 ns).

On the sky130 folded symmetric FIR, keep the 8 symmetric pre-adders and acc_width 29 instead of dropping symmetry and narrowing to 28, because that area-trimming move raised LUT 5429→9180 (+3751), lowered Fmax 204.67→199.03 MHz (−5.6 MHz), and lost feasibility while the multiplier-internal adder critical path stayed limiting.

When a folded symmetric sky130 FIR is feasible at 204.67 MHz but multiplier-bound by the 5.47 ns operand-register -> 12x12 carry-save -> product-register path, dropping only the off-path input boundary register (12 FF) while keeping pipe_in/sum_tree is timing-neutral and area-costly (205.3 MHz, +0.6 MHz, +309 LUT), so reserve pipeline changes for the multiplier path rather than trimming boundary registers.

When transposing a sky130 folded symmetric FIR to fold=1 for throughput, if the symmetric pre-adder carry chain limits timing, switch to non-symmetric to remove the pre-adder from the multiplier input and drop acc_width from 29 to 28, gaining +7.9 MHz (205.3->213.16 MHz) and -53 LUT with no DSP change, at the cost of doubling multipliers from 8 to 16.

On sky130, when a fold=1 transposed FIR is at its sample-rate cap with a critical adder and only ~13 MHz margin (213.16 MHz, 5685 LUTs), do not trim the off-critical-path input register for area: it raised LUTs to 5959 (+274) and dropped Fmax to 205.46 MHz (-7.7 MHz) with no DSP change, because the adder array stayed critical and the exposed input path added logic/routing overhead.
